title: tracing tests: assert the trace count before looping over traces or spans so an empty get_traces() cannot pass vacuously
answers: My tracing test passes even though no trace was recorded, why?
How should I write a test that checks span attributes on every trace returned by get_traces()?
Which test file has the span description and default-none tests?
body:
Path: tests/tracing/test_fluent.py:test_span_description_default_none and the other span-description tests read traces back with get_traces() and then check span attributes on each trace.
Rule: Assert the expected count (assert len(traces) == N) before any for-loop over traces or spans. If get_traces() returns an empty list the loop body never executes and the test passes without checking anything.
Constraints: Applies to loop-based assertions over recorded traces in this file. Single-trace tests that index traces[0] already fail on an empty result and need no loop guard.
applies: Test code in tests/tracing that iterates over traces returned by get_traces(); not a runtime behavior change.
says: Trace verification tests pass in automated checks even when no traces were actually captured.
Span descriptions are missing from recorded traces but the test suite reports success.
Automated checks for trace spans pass vacuously when the trace list is completely empty.
Ensure trace validation fails when expected spans or traces are not logged at all.
search: Tracing tests that iterate over traces or spans returned by get_traces() must assert the expected count (assert len(traces) == N) before looping to prevent empty results from passing vacuously. This applies to test code in tests/tracing/test_fluent.py (such as test_span_description_default_none and other span-description tests) rather than runtime behavior. Single-trace tests that directly index traces[0] already fail on empty results and do not require this count assertion guard.
